The secret information is stored in memory, where the attacker can trigger the victim program to execute by sending characters to its standard input (stdin). The container base image currently ships libgcrypt20 1.10.3-2ubuntu0.2, the fixed release (confirmed by pulling the current base image and checking installed package versions directly, since this OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the base image resolves to at build time). Independent of the version, checking the Java runtime's own library linkage shows it does not link libgcrypt at all; the package is pulled in only as a dependency of GnuPG/apt/systemd tooling (gpg, gpgv, gpg-agent, dirmngr, libapt-pkg, libsystemd0), none of which Liquibase invokes. Java uses its own JCE crypto providers, not system libgcrypt.

statements.status_notes: Denial-of-service on Windows applications using Netty. Netty attempts to read OS identification files even on Windows systems where they don't natively exist. An attacker with local access can create an oversized (>1GB) file at these paths, causing Netty to load it into memory and exhaust the JVM heap, crashing the application.
statements.impact_statement: Netty's PlatformDependent unconditionally attempts to read /etc/os-release and /usr/lib/os-release-style paths for OS identification, including on Windows where these paths don't natively exist. Exploitation requires an attacker who already has local filesystem write access sufficient to plant a >1GB file at one of these root-level paths ahead of JVM startup — a precondition that itself requires the host to already be compromised at a level exceeding what this DoS provides. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver; Liquibase does not read or configure these paths itself.

statements.status_notes: Git, before versions 2.48.1, 2.47.3, 2.46.5, 2.45.4, and 2.44.3, has a vulnerability where a Git client using a terminal that supports ANSI escape sequences can have those sequences, when written to the sideband channel used by the server to transmit informational or error messages during clone/fetch/push, misrepresent the state of a fetch/pull/push or otherwise mislead the user into executing untrusted scripts.
statements.impact_statement: Exploitation requires cloning, fetching from, or pushing to an attacker-controlled Git remote that injects malicious ANSI escape sequences over the sideband channel. Liquibase runtime code never shells out to `git clone`, `git fetch`, or `git push` against any remote — a stronger, structural argument than merely trusting a given remote. A source review confirmed no process/exec invocation of git anywhere in Liquibase's runtime code. The only git usage in this repo at all is CI's own checkout step, which clones this repository's own trusted GitHub remote with a git binary version pinned by the runner image, not by this repo — not the exploit scenario this CVE describes.

NOTE: it may also be argued that system administrators should not have assigned uids, within local networks, that are within the range that can occur in /etc/subuid.
statements.impact_statement: shadow-utils establishes a default /etc/subuid range (uid 100000-165535 for the first user account) that can realistically collide with the uids of users on a network, enabling account takeover via newuidmap when a host operator has configured rootless user-namespace remapping. This is a host-level configuration concern; this image never sets up subuid ranges or invokes newuidmap itself.

statements.status_notes: IO::Uncompress::Unzip versions before 2.215 for Perl propagate an uncaught exception when parsing a zip header with a malformed DOS date. The _dosToUnixTime() function calls Time::Local::timelocal() without an eval guard; a header whose date field decodes to an out-of-range month, day, or hour causes the exception to propagate out of the caller, which expects undef plus an error variable instead.
statements.impact_statement: Perl's IO::Uncompress::Unzip propagates an uncaught exception when a zip header's DOS date field decodes to an out-of-range value. The container's entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI directly (a Java process, not a shell script that shells out to Perl), and a source review found no invocation of perl or any Perl module anywhere in Liquibase's build or runtime. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

Spring Boot EndpointRequest.to() creates a security matcher for null/** instead of the actuator endpoint path when the endpoint is disabled. Requires a running Spring Boot web application with Spring Security and actuator endpoint configuration. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context, never runs an HTTP server, never exposes actuator endpoints, and never configures Spring Security.

Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts the Tomcat HTTP server, never deploys any servlet, and never opens any network port. Same precondition as CVE-2024-47535 — requires an attacker who already has local filesystem write access to plant the malicious file before JVM startup. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver; Liquibase does not read or configure these paths itself.

Requires a running Spring application with method-level security annotations on generic type hierarchies. Liquibase is a CLI tool that does not use Spring Security, does not enable @EnableMethodSecurity, and does not start a Spring application context. The spring-core artifact is a transitive dependency.

statements.status_notes: GNU Tar through 1.35 allows file overwrite via directory traversal in crafted TAR archives, with a certain two-step process. First, the victim must extract an archive that contains a ../ symlink to a critical directory. Second, the victim must extract an archive that contains a critical file, specified via a relative pathname that begins with the symlink name and ends with that critical file's name. Here, the extraction follows the symlink and overwrites the critical file. This bypasses the protection mechanism of "Member name contains '..'" that would occur for a single TAR archive that attempted to specify the critical file via a ../ approach. For example, the first archive can contain "x -> ../../../../../home/victim/.ssh" and the second archive can contain x/authorized_keys. This can affect server applications that automatically extract any number of user-supplied TAR archives, and were relying on the blocking of traversal. This can also affect software installation processes in which "tar xf" is run more than once.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports tar 1.35+dfsg-3build1, below Ubuntu's fixed 1.35+dfsg-3ubuntu0.2, but this issue requires extracting attacker-supplied TAR archives more than once into the same directory. Liquibase Secure invokes GNU tar exactly once during image build to unpack its own SHA-256-verified release archive and does not invoke tar at container runtime.

This CVE requires setuptools to process package inputs; no package installation or processing occurs at runtime.

Denial of service via excessive memory consumption in Tomcat multipart upload processing. Requires sending a crafted multipart/form-data HTTP POST to a running Tomcat instance. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server and never accepts HTTP requests. The multipart parsing code path is completely inactive.

Denial of service via HTTP/2 stream reset memory leak in Tomcat. Requires an HTTP/2 connection to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never enables HTTP/2, and accepts no inbound network connections.

Liquibase does not configure channelBinding=require in any default configuration. The vulnerable enforcement code path in ConnectionFactoryImpl.doAuthentication() is not reachable under Liquibase's default configuration.

Denial of service via integer overflow in Tomcat multipart upload file size limit validation. Requires sending a crafted multipart HTTP upload to a running Tomcat server. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server and never processes inbound HTTP requests or multipart uploads.

statements.impact_statement: GNU coreutils' sort utility has a heap buffer under-read reachable only via the traditional key-specification syntax (+POS1[.C1][OPTS]) with an out-of-range character position. The container's build steps and runtime entrypoint use only rm, ln, mkdir, chown, chmod, wget, tar, unzip, and sha256sum — a source review found no invocation of sort anywhere in this repository's Docker build or runtime path. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships coreutils 9.4-3ubuntu6.3, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u461, 8u461-perf, 11.0.28, 17.0.16, 21.0.8, 25; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.16 and 21.0.8; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.15.

Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2) and runs the CLI through docker/Dockerfile:68, not an Oracle Java SE or GraalVM client runtime. The Oracle client environment required by the advisory is absent in this deployment.

statements.impact_statement: A scanner flagged com.nimbusds:nimbus-jose-jwt@10.0.1 as reachable through the com.azure:azure-identity dependency chain used by the Azure extension. Resolving the actual dependency tree shows azure-identity 1.18.4 pulls com.microsoft.azure:msal4j 1.23.1, and msal4j's only reference to com.nimbusds (oauth2-oidc-sdk, which itself depends on nimbus-jose-jwt) is declared with test scope in msal4j's own POM — a test-scope dependency does not propagate to a downstream consumer's compile/runtime classpath. Resolving the dependency tree for io.netty and com.nimbusds artifacts across every module that pulls azure-identity or msal4j transitively (the Azure extension, and the Databricks and MongoDB commercial extensions, which carry defensive ProGuard keep/dontwarn rules referencing com.nimbusds left over from an earlier dependency configuration) confirms zero resolved com.nimbusds:nimbus-jose-jwt artifacts anywhere in this repository's build. The scanner's finding does not correspond to an actual dependency in this codebase.

Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP/2 server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport.

Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server, never configures the Rewrite Valve, and never accepts HTTP requests.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous event-driven network application framework. In versions 4.1.124.Final, and 4.2.0.Alpha3 through 4.2.4.Final, Netty incorrectly accepts standalone newline characters (LF) as a chunk-size line terminator, regardless of a preceding carriage return (CR), instead of requiring CRLF per HTTP/1.1 standards. When combined with reverse proxies that parse LF differently, attackers can craft requests that the proxy sees as one request but Netty processes as two, enabling request smuggling. Fixed in versions 4.1.125.Final and 4.2.5.Final.
statements.impact_statement: Verified against the actual published Liquibase Secure release (not just this source tree): every bundled jar resolves netty-codec-http past the 4.1.125.Final/4.2.5.Final fix line (the AWS extension and Cassandra extension ship 4.1.136.Final, the Azure extension ships 4.1.135.Final, and the Couchbase client's shaded copy ships 4.2.16.Final). As secondary defense-in-depth, this CVE affects Netty's server-side HTTP chunk-size parser; a source review found no references to HttpObjectDecoder, HttpServerCodec, ServerBootstrap, or NioServerSocketChannel anywhere in this repository, so the vulnerable server-side parser path would not be reachable even independent of version.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous event-driven network application framework. In netty-codec-compression versions 4.1.124.Final and below, and netty-codec versions 4.2.4.Final and below, specially crafted input can cause BrotliDecoder and certain other decompression decoders to allocate a large number of reachable byte buffers, leading to denial of service. Fixed in 4.1.125.Final of netty-codec and 4.2.5.Final of netty-codec-compression.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in netty-codec 4.1.125.Final / netty-codec-compression 4.2.5.Final; this repository's current build already resolves netty-codec 4.1.136.Final via the Azure and Cassandra extensions' Netty dependency chains, past the fix line. Liquibase does not accept compressed HTTP payloads from untrusted clients, and a source review found no code referencing BrotliDecoder, BrotliEncoder, BrotliOptions, or io.netty.handler.codec.compression.Brotli — the vulnerable decompression path is not exercised, regardless of version.

statements.status_notes: Due to the design of the name constraint checking algorithm, the processing time of some inputs scale non-linearly with respect to the size of the certificate. This affects programs which validate arbitrary certificate chains.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/x509 name-constraint vulnerability. NVD fixes the 1.25 line in Go 1.25.3 and the 1.24 line in Go 1.24.9; the scanner reported go1.25.1 for this image. Liquibase Secure only installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (docker/Dockerfile:39-55), and the entrypoint only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). Repo-wide source greps found no crypto/x509, SystemCertPool, or CertPool usage in application code, so the arbitrary certificate-chain path described by the advisory is not exercised.

statements.status_notes: Validating certificate chains which contain DSA public keys can cause programs to panic, due to a interface cast that assumes they implement the Equal method. This affects programs which validate arbitrary certificate chains.
statements.impact_statement: Validating certificate chains with DSA public keys is not a reachable input path for Liquibase Secure. NVD fixes this in Go 1.25.2, but the Docker image only installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (docker/Dockerfile:35-55) and the entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). Upstream lpm uses a default http.Client for downloads with no custom RootCAs or PEM loading logic (/tmp/gh-aw/agent/lpm/internal/app/utils/Http.go:13-25), so the arbitrary certificate-chain path described by the advisory is not exercised here.

False positive due to classifier confusion. Trivy reads the JAR's internal pom.properties which reports version 13.2.1 (without the jre11 classifier), causing a false version comparison. The installed JAR is 13.2.1.jre11 which contains the fix. Microsoft's non-standard Maven versioning uses a classifier suffix instead of a standard version bump.

statements.status_notes: libexpat in Expat before 2.7.2 allows attackers to trigger large dynamic memory allocations via a small document that is submitted for parsing.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to call libexpat's parsing API on a crafted document to trigger large dynamic allocations. Liquibase Secure parses changelogs using the JVM's own bundled XML parser and never links against or calls system libexpat.

statements.status_notes: The html.parser.HTMLParser class had worst-case quadratic complexity when processing certain crafted malformed inputs at end-of-file, potentially leading to an amplified denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: Liquibase Secure bundles a GraalPy-based embedded Python runtime so that customers can author custom policy-check scripts with full access to the Python standard library, including html.parser. None of the check scripts Liquibase ships and runs by default import html.parser — they parse changeset SQL with a different library. Triggering this issue requires a customer to deliberately author and configure their own custom check script that imports html.parser and feeds it attacker-controlled data; Liquibase creates no such exposure on its own, and no shipped check performs this action.

statements.status_notes: GNU ncurses up to 6.5-20250322 has a stack-based buffer overflow in postprocess_termcap (tinfo/parse_entry.c) due to improper bounds checking during termcap entry processing, allowing a local attacker to trigger the overflow via a crafted termcap file, leading to denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: A stack-based buffer overflow in ncurses' termcap entry parsing requires a local attacker able to supply a crafted termcap file or TERM/TERMINFO value processed by an interactive terminal session. The Liquibase Secure container runs the CLI non-interactively via its entrypoint, without accepting untrusted local termcap input; TERM is set by the container orchestration layer, not by an untrusted local actor. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships libncursesw6 6.4+20240113-1ubuntu2.2, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: The processing time for parsing some invalid inputs scales non-linearly with respect to the size of the input. This affects programs which parse untrusted PEM inputs.
statements.impact_statement: Untrusted PEM parsing is not a reachable input path for Liquibase Secure. NVD fixes this in Go 1.25.2, but the Docker image only installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (docker/Dockerfile:35-55) and the entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). Upstream lpm uses a default http.Client for downloads with no PEM parsing or certificate-loader code (/tmp/gh-aw/agent/lpm/internal/app/utils/Http.go:13-25), so the invalid-PEM parsing path described by the advisory is not exercised here.

statements.status_notes: The Reader.ReadResponse function constructs a response string through repeated string concatenation of lines. When the number of lines in a response is large, this can cause excessive CPU consumption.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib Reader.ReadResponse CPU exhaustion vulnerability fixed in Go 1.24.8 and 1.25.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), download it from the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 release (docker/Dockerfile:49), and the corresponding upstream liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3 declares go 1.25.10, which includes the fix. GitHub code search for liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 found no direct ReadResponse, net/textproto, or net/http usage, so the vulnerable API is not directly reachable from lpm source.

statements.status_notes: The ParseAddress function constructs domain-literal address components through repeated string concatenation. When parsing large domain-literal components, this can cause excessive CPU consumption.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib ParseAddress CPU exhaustion vulnerability fixed in Go 1.24.8 and 1.25.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), download it from the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 release (docker/Dockerfile:49), and the corresponding upstream liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3 declares go 1.25.10, which includes the fix. GitHub code search for liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 found no direct ParseAddress or net/mail usage, so the vulnerable email parsing API is not reachable from lpm source.

statements.status_notes: Building a malicious file with cmd/go can cause can cause a write to an attacker-controlled file with partial control of the file content. The "#cgo pkg-config:" directive in a Go source file provides command-line arguments to provide to the Go pkg-config command. An attacker can provide a "--log-file" argument to this directive, causing pkg-config to write to an attacker-controlled location.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib cmd/go build-time smuggling vulnerability fixed in Go 1.24.12 and 1.25.6. The Secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and the only runtime invocation is `lpm add mysql --global` behind INSTALL_MYSQL (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4 and docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5). Repo-wide grep found no runtime `go build`, `go mod`, `GOTOOLCHAIN`, `GOMODPROXY`, `GOSUMDB`, `pkg-config`, or `cgo` usage, so the vulnerable cmd/go path is not reachable.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. In versions prior to 4.1.129.Final and 4.2.8.Final, the io.netty.handler.codec.http.HttpRequestEncoder has a CRLF injection via the request URI when constructing a request, leading to request smuggling when HttpRequestEncoder is used without proper sanitization of the URI. Fixed in versions 4.1.129.Final and 4.2.8.Final.
statements.impact_statement: Verified against the actual published Liquibase Secure release (not just this source tree): every bundled jar resolves netty-codec-http past the 4.1.129.Final/4.2.8.Final fix line (the AWS extension and Cassandra extension ship 4.1.136.Final, the Azure extension ships 4.1.135.Final, and the Couchbase client's shaded copy ships 4.2.16.Final). As secondary defense-in-depth, a source review found no references to HttpRequestEncoder anywhere in this repository, so this repository does not directly wire the vulnerable request-encoding class either.

statements.status_notes: The infocmp command-line tool in ncurses before 6.5-20251213 has a stack-based buffer overflow in analyze_string in progs/infocmp.c.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libncursesw6 6.4+20240113-1ubuntu2, below Ubuntu's fixed 6.4+20240113-1ubuntu2.1, but this issue is in ncurses' infocmp utility. The stock Liquibase Secure image runs the Liquibase CLI non-interactively, and a review of its build and runtime path found no invocation of infocmp or processing of attacker-supplied termcap or terminfo input.

statements.status_notes: A use-after-free vulnerability exists in libcurl when an application configures an HTTP/2 stream-dependency tree via CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS or CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS_E, subsequently invokes curl_easy_reset(), and finally terminates the handle with curl_easy_cleanup(). During this final cleanup phase, libcurl attempts to access and modify an internal structure that was already freed during the reset operation.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.11, but this issue affects applications that configure libcurl stream dependencies and then reset and clean up the same handle. Liquibase Secure's build path uses wget for downloads, not curl, and a review of the secure-image build and stock runtime path found no use of curl or the affected libcurl APIs.

statements.status_notes: An integer underflow vulnerability was found in MIT krb5 in the berval2tl_data() function in plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ ldap_principal2.c. The function performs an unsigned subtraction (bv_len - 2) without a prior bounds check. When bv_len is 0 or 1, the subtraction wraps to a large value which is then truncated to uint16_t. The subsequent malloc succeeds and memcpy reads up to 65534 bytes from a 0-1 byte buffer, resulting in a heap out-of-bounds read. The attack vector involves a malicious or compromised LDAP KDB backend returning a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2, triggering the underflow when the KDC or kadmind reads principal data.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libgssapi-krb5-2 1.20.1-6ubuntu2.6, below Ubuntu's fixed 1.20.1-6ubuntu2.7, but this integer-underflow flaw is in MIT krb5's LDAP KDB backend when a KDC or kadmind reads malformed krbExtraData from a malicious or compromised LDAP backend. Liquibase Secure ships the package only as part of the inherited base image and runs the Liquibase CLI, not a Kerberos KDC or kadmind with an LDAP KDB backend.

statements.status_notes: Using libcurl to do a transfer to a specific HTTP origin with Digest authentication and then changing the origin to a different one for a second transfer while reusing the same handle causes libcurl to wrongly pass on the Authorization header field meant for the first origin to the second. This flaw does not affect the curl command-line tool.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw is in libcurl's handle-reuse behavior: reusing the same handle for Digest-authenticated transfers to two different origins can leak the first origin's Authorization header to the second. Per curl's own advisory, this does not affect the curl command-line tool at all — only applications that reuse a libcurl handle across origins. The container's build steps use wget, not curl, for downloads, and the runtime entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI — a source review found no invocation of curl anywhere in this repository's Docker build or runtime path. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships curl 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.13, newer than the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Socket versions before 2.041 for Perl have an out-of-bounds heap read. pack_ip_mreq_source() in Socket.xs validates argument lengths in the wrong order, so a source address shorter than 4 bytes is not rejected and the copy reads up to 3 bytes past the end of its buffer, leaking adjacent heap memory into the packed structure.
statements.impact_statement: An out-of-bounds heap read exists in Perl's Socket module (pack_ip_mreq_source() in Socket.xs) when an application calls it with a multicast source address shorter than 4 bytes. Liquibase never invokes Perl or any Perl module (see the CVE-2025-15649 assessment on this same subcomponent for the reachability evidence). This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Perl through version 5.43.9 has a regex overflow flaw. When an alternation compiled into a trie by Perl_study_chunk contains more than 65,535 branches, a 16-bit delta field overflows and the trie's match decision table is silently truncated with no warning, causing the regex to return both false positives and false negatives.
statements.impact_statement: Perl's regex compiler silently truncates its match table when an alternation has more than 65,535 branches, producing incorrect (false-positive and false-negative) pattern matches — a risk only when such a regex gates an access-control or input-filtering decision. Liquibase never invokes Perl or any Perl module (see the CVE-2025-15649 assessment on this same subcomponent for the reachability evidence), so no Liquibase security control is implemented via a Perl regex. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.4, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.85, Lazy ASN.1 sequence forcing resets nesting-depth guard. This issue also affects Bouncy Castle for Java LTS before 2.73.12, and Bouncy Castle for Java FIPS (BC-FJA) before bc-fips 1.0.2.7 (1.0.X series), 2.0.2 (2.0.X series) and 2.1.3 (2.1.X series).
statements.impact_statement: This affected bcprov-jdk18on before 1.85. This repository now ships org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on:1.85, past the fixed version, as defense-in-depth. Independent of version, a source review found zero direct `import org.bouncycastle.` usage anywhere in this codebase, and zero references to LazyEncodedSequence, ASN1StreamParser, ASN1InputStream, BERSequenceParser, DLSequenceParser, or LazyConstructionEnumeration. The only Bouncy Castle usage in production code is Snowflake private-key loading through a shaded `net.snowflake.client.jdbc.internal.org.bouncycastle.*` namespace — a different package entirely from the standalone bcprov-jdk18on artifact this CVE affects, and one that never touches the vulnerable ASN.1 parsing classes.

statements.status_notes: A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. During nested partition probing, the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, and UnixWare partition probers cache a raw pointer to a parent partition entry in a dynamically allocated array; when subsequent partition additions reallocate the array, the pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. An attacker who can present a crafted block device image can trigger this without user interaction, since libblkid is invoked automatically by udev/udisks as root on block-device hot-plug events.
statements.impact_statement: This use-after-free in libblkid's nested partition probing (BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, UnixWare probers) is triggered automatically by udev/udisks as root on a block-device hot-plug event, such as a USB insertion or a loop-mounted disk image — containers do not perform hot-plug block-device management, and a source review of the Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no invocation of udev, udisks, blkid, or any partition-probing tool; the stock container's entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships bsdutils 1:2.39.3-9ubuntu6.6, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: A flaw in the libcurl SASL negotiation for LDAP authentication allows an incomplete handshake sequence to be misinterpreted as a successful cryptographic verification. An attacker executing a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack can inject a premature or shortcut response that bypasses complete peer validation.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to use libcurl's SASL negotiation for LDAP authentication. Liquibase Secure's runtime process tree never links against libcurl and never performs LDAP authentication via libcurl; curl ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: A flaw was found in p11-kit. The RPC message attribute parsing functions form a mutually-recursive call chain with no recursion depth limit when processing nested CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE, CKA_UNWRAP_TEMPLATE, and CKA_DERIVE_TEMPLATE attributes. An unauthenticated attacker with local access to the p11-kit RPC Unix domain socket can send a specially crafted request with deeply nested template attributes, causing stack exhaustion and crashing the p11-kit server process and its dependent services.
statements.impact_statement: The reported package is inherited from the container base image. Exploitation requires a running p11-kit RPC Unix domain socket and local access to that service. Liquibase Secure does not start p11-kit or any auxiliary daemon: the container entrypoint only execs the Liquibase CLI, and a source review of the Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no reference to p11-kit or pkcs11. Without a p11-kit RPC service/socket in the deployed container, the required runtime environment is absent.

statements.status_notes: Local unprivileged users can terminate arbitrary local processes via a systemd-oomd IPC API due to a missing path traversal validation.
statements.impact_statement: This issue is in systemd-oomd's IPC API. The Liquibase Secure image inherits Ubuntu packages from the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image (`docker/Dockerfile:2`) and creates a static liquibase user with useradd rather than running systemd-managed services (`docker/Dockerfile:5`). The container entrypoint only execs a requested command or the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no references to oomd or systemd-oomd, so the required systemd-oomd IPC service is absent from the stock container environment.

statements.status_notes: GNU Wget does not validate the IP address provided by an FTP PASV response while operating in FTP passive mode. A malicious FTP server, or an HTTP server that redirects to an FTP URL, can exploit this behavior to redirect Wget's data connection to an arbitrary IP address and port. This allows an attacker to forge server-side requests from the machine running Wget, potentially accessing localhost services or internal network resources.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports wget 1.21.4-1ubuntu4.1, below Ubuntu's fixed 1.21.4-1ubuntu4.4, but this issue requires Wget to follow an attacker-controlled FTP passive-mode data connection. Liquibase Secure uses wget only during image build to fetch its release tarball and the lpm zip over HTTPS, and it does not invoke wget at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: An issue was found in Python's incremental HTML parser (html.parser.HTMLParser). When application code repeatedly feeds small pieces of attacker-controlled data into the parser while an HTML construct remains unterminated, the parser can be driven to consume disproportionate CPU time, resulting in a denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: Liquibase Secure bundles a GraalPy-based embedded Python runtime so that customers can author custom policy-check scripts with full access to the Python standard library, including html.parser. None of the check scripts Liquibase ships and runs by default import html.parser — they parse changeset SQL with a different library. Triggering this issue requires a customer to deliberately author and configure their own custom check script that imports html.parser and feeds it attacker-controlled data; Liquibase creates no such exposure on its own, and no shipped check performs this action.

statements.status_notes: Perl versions through 5.45.1 have out-of-bounds heap reads and writes during regular expression matching via an undersized superlinear cache in S_regmatch. A caller that matches an attacker-controlled subject of the required size and pattern shape can crash the process or corrupt heap memory.
statements.impact_statement: This regex-engine heap read/write flaw is reachable only when an application performs Perl regular-expression matching on attacker supplied subject strings. The container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase Java CLI directly (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`), and a focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no perl invocation. The vulnerable Perl regex path is therefore not reachable from the stock Liquibase Secure runtime.

statements.status_notes: GNU wget is vulnerable to denial of service in its FTP OPIE/S-KEY authentication functionality. The server-supplied sequence number from the FTP challenge line is used as an iteration count for an MD5 key- derivation loop without any upper bound validation. A malicious FTP server or a network attacker positioned to intercept FTP traffic can send a crafted OPIE challenge with a sequence number near INT_MAX, causing wget to perform up to approximately 2.1 billion MD5 computations and suspend for some time. The --timeout option does not mitigate this because it applies only to network I/O, not CPU computation. This issue was fixed in commit e9697d98e7249b0f68a6be040a4f3dcc5bc101fa
statements.impact_statement: wget FTP OPIE/S-KEY authentication denial-of-service issue, with an upstream patch not yet backported to Ubuntu noble. wget is only invoked at Docker build time against hardcoded, sha256-verified URLs (docker/Dockerfile:27, docker/Dockerfile:55); never invoked at runtime, and this image never performs FTP transfers.

statements.status_notes: systemd-homed contains a local privilege escalation bug via arbitrary system group addition to a local, logged in, homed-managed user.
statements.impact_statement: This privilege-escalation flaw requires systemd-homed to manage a local, logged-in user. The Liquibase Secure image creates its liquibase user statically with useradd during image build (`docker/Dockerfile:5`) and the entrypoint only execs the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no homed or systemd-homed references, so the required systemd-homed runtime environment is absent.

statements.status_notes: Passing an effectively empty string to the ",ccs=" syntax extension of the mode argument in the fopen function in the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the function is attacker controlled. This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common GNU/Linux distributions.
statements.impact_statement: This heap buffer overflow requires an application to call glibc's fopen function with an attacker-controlled mode string containing an effectively empty ",ccs=" syntax extension. Liquibase Secure's runtime never constructs fopen mode strings from external input; the JVM's own file I/O does not use this glibc idiom.

statements.status_notes: A TOCTOU (Time-of-Check Time-of-Use) vulnerability in GNU tar's incremental dumpdir 'X' rename handling allows a local attacker with write access to a directory being backed up to influence the restore process if the attacker has access to the system where the restore is being performed. During restoration, files or directories may be created, renamed or overwritten outside the intended extraction directory.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires GNU tar's incremental dumpdir mode and a local attacker who can race the restore process on the target system. Liquibase Secure's Dockerfile invokes tar exactly once, at image build time, to extract its own trusted release tarball in plain (non-incremental) mode; tar is never invoked at container runtime on any input.

statements.status_notes: A flaw was found in GNU tar. When extracting an archive with the --one-top-level option, hardlink targets are not confined to the designated top-level directory and may resolve relative to the extraction working directory. A crafted archive can create hardlinks that escape the intended boundary and, when combined with a preexisting symbolic link under the working directory, may allow writing outside the intended directory.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw is triggered by extracting a crafted archive with GNU tar's --one-top-level option. Liquibase Secure's Dockerfile invokes tar exactly once, at image build time, to extract its own trusted release tarball with no --one-top-level flag; tar is never invoked at container runtime on any input, let alone attacker-controlled archives.

statements.status_notes: A flaw in libcurl's handling of HTTP/2 Server Push streams, when the parent handle is set to share connections with other handles, can lead to use-after-free in the cleanup process.
statements.impact_statement: This use-after-free requires an application to configure libcurl handles to share connections while processing HTTP/2 Server Push streams. Liquibase Secure's runtime process tree never links against libcurl; curl ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: A flaw was found in p11-kit. A local attacker, or one with equivalent access to a reachable RPC channel, could exploit an integer overflow in nested attribute parsing and cause a heap out-of-bounds write that crashes the p11-kit RPC parsing process. This vulnerability is only exploitable on 32-bit systems.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw is in p11-kit's RPC message parser and requires a reachable p11-kit RPC channel. The stock Liquibase Secure container does not start p11-kit or any auxiliary daemon: the entrypoint only execs a requested command or the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`), and a focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no p11-kit or pkcs11 references. Without a p11-kit RPC service/socket, the required runtime environment is absent.

statements.status_notes: Perl versions from 5.9.4 before 5.41.9 can produce incorrect regular expression match results when a stale failure flag ends the Aho-Corasick prescan early in S_find_byclass, which can make access or filtering decisions wrong.
statements.impact_statement: This incorrect-match issue affects Perl's regex prescan logic and is relevant only when an application performs Perl regular-expression matching on attacker-controlled data and then makes a security decision from the result. The container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase Java CLI directly (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`), and a focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no perl invocation. The vulnerable Perl regex path is not reachable in the stock runtime.

statements.status_notes: Calling strfmon and strfmon_l in the GNU C Library version 2.38 to 2.44 can write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer when a conversion uses right-justified width padding. At the time of publication, no network-facing application impact is known.
statements.impact_statement: This glibc flaw is reachable only through application calls to strfmon or strfmon_l with a vulnerable right-justified width-padding pattern. The Liquibase Secure image inherits the OS package from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (`docker/Dockerfile:2`) and the container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles, entrypoint scripts, and application source found no references to strfmon or strfmon_l, so the vulnerable API path is not reachable from the stock Liquibase Secure runtime.

statements.status_notes: Calling tdelete on a sufficiently deep tree in the GNU C Library version 2.1 to 2.44 may write one pointer past the end of an alloca-allocated array on the stack, which may crash the application. No affected application in common distributions has been identified.
statements.impact_statement: This glibc flaw requires an application to use tsearch/tdelete on a very deep tree. The Liquibase Secure image inherits the OS package from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (`docker/Dockerfile:2`) and the container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles, entrypoint scripts, and application source found no references to tsearch or tdelete, so the vulnerable API path is not reachable from the stock Liquibase Secure runtime.

statements.status_notes: A flaw in libcurl makes it wrongly reuse an HTTP connection setup for a given hostname using Negotiate authentication, when the initial request is done using empty credentials. This can make user B's request get sent over user A's previously authenticated connection.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw is a libcurl API-level connection-reuse bug: an application linked against libcurl must issue Negotiate-authenticated requests with empty initial credentials for the vulnerable connection-pooling logic to trigger. The Liquibase Secure container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase Java CLI; a review of the JVM's own native library dependencies and the container's runtime entrypoint found no linkage against libcurl anywhere in the process tree. curl ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

urllib3 vulnerability. urllib3 is bundled as a transitive dependency within GraalVM Python extensions but its HTTP client functionality is never invoked at runtime. All Python packages are pre-installed at build time via Maven graalpy-maven-plugin; no HTTP requests are made via Python at runtime.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: AWT, JavaFX). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u471, 8u471-b50, 8u471-perf, 11.0.29, 17.0.17, 21.0.9, 25.0.1; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.17 and 21.0.9; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.16. Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker and while the vulnerability is in Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change). Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized creation, deletion or modification access to critical data or all Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition accessible data.

Incomplete OCSP verification in Tomcat's FFM/OpenSSL TLS integration. Requires an active TLS listener with client certificate authentication and OCSP validation configured. Go stdlib vulnerability in the Docker base image. Liquibase is a Java application and does not execute Go code at runtime. The Go binary is part of Docker base image tooling and is not invoked by Liquibase.

Go stdlib cmd/go code smuggling via SWIG file names is not reachable in Liquibase Secure images. The secure Docker image installs lpm from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:39) and the runtime entrypoint only uses lpm to add mysql when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4). statements.status_notes: Arithmetic over induction variables in loops were not correctly checked for underflow or overflow. As a result, the compiler would allow invalid indexing at runtime, potentially leading to memory corruption.
statements.impact_statement: Go arithmetic-overflow compiler bug in loop induction variables is only reachable while compiling Go code with the toolchain. Liquibase Secure installs lpm from a release ZIP (`docker/Dockerfile:39`) and the runtime entrypoint only invokes lpm to add mysql when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4`). This image does not run the Go compiler or build Go code at runtime.

Go compiler memory corruption in pointer unwrapping is not reachable in Liquibase Secure images. The secure Docker image installs lpm from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:39) and the runtime entrypoint only uses lpm to add mysql when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4). statements.status_notes: (*x509.Certificate).VerifyHostname previously called matchHostnames in a loop over all DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. This caused strings.Split(host, ".") to execute repeatedly on the same input hostname. With a large DNS SAN list, verification costs scaled quadratically based on the number of SAN entries multiplied by the hostname's label count. Because x509.Verify validates hostnames before building the certificate chain, this overhead occurred even for untrusted certificates.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/x509 VerifyHostname quadratic complexity vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.11 and 1.26.4. The scanner reported affected Go stdlib versions in the lpm helper bundled in published Liquibase Secure Docker images. The Secure Dockerfile installs lpm as an optional helper (docker/Dockerfile:35, docker/Dockerfile:49), but the Docker entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is explicitly configured (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4); otherwise it executes the Java Liquibase CLI directly (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119). A focused grep across the Docker runtime files found no direct VerifyHostname, Certificate.Verify, matchHostnames, HostnameError, or crypto/x509 usage. Defense in depth: current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.5 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 declares go 1.25.11 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

statements.status_notes: zlib before 1.3.2 allows CPU consumption via crc32_combine64 and crc32_combine_gen64 because x2nmodp can do right shifts within a loop that has no termination condition.
statements.impact_statement: This zlib issue is tied to the crc32_combine64, crc32_combine_gen64, and x2nmodp code path. The Liquibase Secure image inherits the OS package from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (`docker/Dockerfile:2`) and the container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles, entrypoint scripts, and application source found no references to those zlib APIs, so the vulnerable code path is not reachable from the stock runtime.

statements.status_notes: util-linux before 2.41.4 has a TOCTOU vulnerability in the SUID /usr/bin/mount binary when setting up loop devices. Exploitation requires an /etc/fstab entry with user,loop options whose path is attacker-writable and a SUID mount binary.
statements.impact_statement: This util-linux mount race requires a SUID /usr/bin/mount binary plus an /etc/fstab entry with user,loop options pointing to a user-writable path. The stock Liquibase Secure container's entrypoint only execs a requested command or the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`), and a focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no references to /etc/fstab, /usr/bin/mount, user,loop, blkid, udisks, or udev. The required loop-mount configuration is absent from the stock container.

Nesting depth constraint bypass in Jackson Core 3.x UTF8DataInputJsonParser and ReaderBasedJsonParser. maxNestingDepth from StreamReadConstraints is not enforced, allowing a deeply nested JSON document to cause StackOverflowError. Liquibase is a CLI tool that only parses JSON from trusted, operator-controlled configuration files and changelog artifacts. It does not expose any JSON parsing endpoint to remote or untrusted input. As established in the prior assessment of GHSA-2m67-wjpj-xhg9, Liquibase does not rely on StreamReadConstraints as a security boundary.

TLS 1.3 cipher suite preference order not preserved in Tomcat's SSL connector configuration. Requires an active TLS connector performing cipher negotiation. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or binds a TLS connector. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; no TLS handshakes occur.

statements.status_notes: Apache Tomcat authentication bypass where OCSP validation soft-fails even when soft-fail is explicitly disabled, allowing revoked client certificates to authenticate.
statements.impact_statement: Authentication bypass due to CLIENT_CERT soft fail misconfiguration in Tomcat's OCSP validation. Requires an active HTTPS connector configured with CLIENT_CERT authentication and an OCSP responder. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that uses picocli for command-line parsing and never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No connector, no authenticator, no OCSP — the code is inert.

Information disclosure via padding oracle vulnerability in Tomcat EncryptInterceptor (clustering component). Requires Tomcat clustering with EncryptInterceptor enabled. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or initializes clustering. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; EncryptInterceptor is never instantiated.

Go stdlib crypto/x509 DoS vulnerability (GO-2026-4947). Detected in the compiled lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) binary built with Go 1.25.8. govulncheck symbol-level analysis confirms the vulnerable code paths are not called by lpm. Fix: DAT-22804 bumps Go to 1.25.9 in liquibase-package-manager, eliminating the vulnerability at the source.

statements.status_notes: Validating certificate chains which use policies is unexpectedly inefficient when certificates in the chain contain a very large number of policy mappings, possibly causing denial of service. This only affects validation of otherwise trusted certificate chains, issued by a root CA in the VerifyOptions.Roots CertPool, or in the system certificate pool.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/x509 certificate policy mapping DoS vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.9 and 1.26.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.3 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.3 declares go 1.25.9 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

Go stdlib internal/syscall/unix Root.Chmod symlink traversal vulnerability. Detected in the compiled lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) binary built with Go 1.25.8. govulncheck symbol-level analysis confirms the vulnerable code paths are not called by lpm. Fix: DAT-22804 bumps Go to 1.25.9 in liquibase-package-manager, eliminating the vulnerability at the source.

statements.status_notes: If one side of the TLS connection sends multiple key update messages post-handshake in a single record, the connection can deadlock, causing uncontrolled consumption of resources. This can lead to a denial of service. This only affects TLS 1.3.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/tls TLS 1.3 key update DoS vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.9 and 1.26.2. Current Docker builds install lpm 0.3.3 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.3 declares go 1.25.9 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix.

statements.status_notes: libexpat before 2.7.5 allows a NULL pointer dereference with empty external parameter entity content.
statements.impact_statement: This NULL pointer dereference requires an application to call libexpat's parser with an empty external parameter entity. Liquibase Secure parses changelogs using the JVM's own bundled XML parser and never links against or calls system libexpat.

statements.status_notes: libexpat before 2.7.5 allows an infinite loop while parsing DTD content.
statements.impact_statement: This infinite loop requires an application to call libexpat's DTD parsing path on crafted DTD content. Liquibase Secure parses changelogs using the JVM's own bundled XML parser and never links against or calls system libexpat.

statements.status_notes: libexpat before 2.7.5 allows a NULL pointer dereference in the function setContext on retry after an earlier out-of-memory condition.
statements.impact_statement: This NULL pointer dereference requires an application to retry libexpat's setContext function after an earlier out-of-memory condition. Liquibase Secure parses changelogs using the JVM's own bundled XML parser and never links against or calls system libexpat.

statements.status_notes: When using LookupCNAME with the cgo DNS resolver, a very long CNAME response can trigger a double-free of C memory and a crash.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib LookupCNAME double-free in the cgo DNS resolver when processing a very long CNAME response. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it downloads Liquibase extension driver JARs from GitHub release assets via HTTP. lpm never calls LookupCNAME — standard HTTP hostname resolution uses LookupIPAddr/LookupHost, not the CNAME-specific API. Additionally, the vulnerability requires the cgo DNS resolver, which is not the default on Linux; the pure-Go DNS resolver is active in the eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble container.

statements.status_notes: When processing HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames, transport will enter an infinite loop of writing CONTINUATION frames if it receives a SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib HTTP/2 transport infinite loop when a server sends SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with a value of 0. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image; it makes HTTP/2 connections to GitHub release servers to download Liquibase extension driver JARs. Exploitation requires a server to send the malformed SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE=0 frame. lpm only connects to trusted GitHub release CDN endpoints (URLs and checksums fixed in docker/Dockerfile:35-55); no attacker- controlled server endpoint exists in lpm's execution path.

statements.status_notes: Enforce a recursion limit in Unmarshal to prevent stack exhaustion when parsing deeply-nested, recursive structures.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib recursion-limit issue in Unmarshal. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. The secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50) and the runtime entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5). The default Liquibase runtime path executes the Java CLI directly, so the Unmarshal path that would process attacker-controlled deeply nested data is not exercised. This assessment also covers the GO-2026-5972 alias.

statements.status_notes: Netty HttpObjectDecoder incorrectly terminates chunk header parsing at \r\n inside quoted strings in chunked transfer encoding extensions, enabling HTTP request smuggling.
statements.impact_statement: HTTP request smuggling via chunked transfer encoding in Netty HTTP codec. This is a server-side vulnerability requiring an attacker to send malicious HTTP/1.1 requests to a Netty HTTP server. Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections. There is no listening socket for an attacker to exploit.

statements.status_notes: See CVE-2026-33870 entry on netty-codec-http. Mirrored here so scanners that flag netty-transport receive the same not_affected statement.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner over-match: the vulnerable code lives in netty-codec-http (see the sibling assessment above). OWASP Dependency-Check and similar CPE-based scanners propagate the CVE onto netty-transport via the broad cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty:* match. netty-transport ships no HTTP/1.1 chunked decoder, so even if it were exposed as a server (which Liquibase is not), the affected code path would not run from this artifact.

statements.status_notes: See CVE-2026-33870 entry on netty-codec-http. Mirrored for sibling transport artifact so scanners receive the same not_affected statement.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner over-match: same root assessment as netty-codec-http (see above). netty-transport-classes-epoll provides Linux epoll(7) native transport classes — no HTTP parser code. The cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty:* CPE causes OWASP to propagate the CVE here. Liquibase does not expose any HTTP server; the vulnerable chunked-encoding decoder is unreachable from this artifact regardless.

statements.status_notes: See CVE-2026-33870 entry on netty-codec-http. Mirrored for sibling transport artifact so scanners receive the same not_affected statement.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner over-match: same root assessment as netty-codec-http (see above). netty-transport-classes-kqueue provides macOS/BSD kqueue(2) native transport classes — no HTTP parser code. CPE-based propagation only.

Liquibase is a database migration CLI tool that does not run an HTTP/2 server. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport. There is no inbound HTTP/2 listener.

statements.status_notes: See CVE-2026-33871 entry on netty-codec-http2. Mirrored here so scanners that flag netty-transport receive the same not_affected statement.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner over-match: the vulnerable code lives in netty-codec-http2 (see the sibling assessment above). OWASP Dependency-Check and similar CPE-based scanners propagate the CVE onto netty-transport via the broad cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty:* match. netty-transport ships no HTTP/2 frame decoder, so even if it were exposed as a server (which Liquibase is not), the affected code path would not run from this artifact.

statements.status_notes: See CVE-2026-33871 entry on netty-codec-http2. Mirrored for sibling transport artifact.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner over-match: same root assessment as netty-codec-http2 (see above). netty-transport-classes-epoll is the Linux epoll native transport — no HTTP/2 frame decoder. CPE-based scanners propagate the CVE here despite the artifact not containing the vulnerable parser.

statements.status_notes: See CVE-2026-33871 entry on netty-codec-http2. Mirrored for sibling transport artifact.
statements.impact_statement: Scanner over-match: same root assessment as netty-codec-http2 (see above). netty-transport-classes-kqueue is the macOS/BSD kqueue native transport — no HTTP/2 frame decoder. CPE-based propagation only.

statements.status_notes: Issue Summary: Cryptographic Message Services (CMS) processing fails to perform sufficient input validation on the cipher and tag length fields of AuthEnvelopedData containers, leading to various potential compromises. Attackers may achieve key-equivalent functionality for a given CMS recipient and/or bypass integrity validation for a given message.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE affects OpenSSL CMS AuthEnvelopedData decryption when attacker-supplied content reaches CMS_decrypt() and the application trusts the result without separate integrity enforcement. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL CMS tooling, and a source review found no references to CMS_decrypt, AuthEnvelopedData, or related CMS processing in the product runtime path. libssl3 is inherited from the base image only, so the vulnerable CMS path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Networking). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u481-perf, 11.0.30, 17.0.18, 21.0.10, 25.0.2, 26; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.18 and 21.0.10; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.17. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.
statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE networking vulnerability. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1), not an Oracle Java SE or GraalVM client distribution. The container runs the Liquibase CLI through docker-entrypoint.sh rather than a sandboxed Java Web Start or applet environment (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8), so the client-only runtime required by the advisory is absent.

Information disclosure via improper encoding in Tomcat JsonAccessLogValve. Requires an active HTTP connector with JsonAccessLogValve configured and non-default relaxedPathChars/relaxedQueryChars values. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; no access log valves are configured or initialized.
