Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Tomcat server or initializes clustering. tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web; Kubernetes cluster membership is never initialized.

statements.status_notes: When an OAuth2 bearer token is used for an HTTP(S) transfer, and that transfer performs a redirect to a second URL, curl could leak that token to the second hostname under some circumstances. If the redirected host has information in the used .netrc file, curl would pass on the bearer token set for the first host also to the second one.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE requires a libcurl-based application to perform an OAuth2 bearer token transfer that follows a redirect while consulting .netrc entries for the redirected host. Liquibase Secure's stock container does not invoke curl or link against libcurl in its own build or runtime path, so the vulnerable token-forwarding path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: curl would wrongly reuse an existing HTTP proxy connection doing CONNECT to a server, even if the new request uses different credentials for the HTTP proxy. The proper behavior is to create or use a separate connection.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE requires a libcurl-based application to reuse an HTTP proxy CONNECT connection while changing proxy credentials between requests. Liquibase Secure's stock container does not invoke curl or link against libcurl in its own build or runtime path, so the vulnerable proxy connection-reuse path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: A buffer overflow in SQLite source snapshots/builds containing Fossil check-in 8bdc0d485e3ad0c7a1e818da66f106951d496b05cbe61d12c2c448f2f24b6d5d and later snapshots/builds can cause denial of service via the ext/misc/sqlar.c sqlarUncompressFunc()/sqlar_uncompress() code path.
statements.impact_statement: This SQLite issue is limited to snapshot builds containing the sqlarUncompressFunc/sqlar_uncompress code path in ext/misc/sqlar.c. The Liquibase Secure image inherits the OS package from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (`docker/Dockerfile:2`) and the container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles, entrypoint scripts, and application source found no references to sqlarUncompressFunc, sqlar_uncompress, sqlite3_value_int64, or sqlite3_malloc, so the vulnerable snapshot-only code path is not reachable from the stock runtime.

statements.status_notes: Well-crafted inputs reaching ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate were able to trigger excessive CPU exhaustion and memory allocations.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib net/mail CPU exhaustion via pathological inputs to ParseAddress, ParseAddressList, and ParseDate. lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image. lpm is a package manager for Liquibase extension drivers and has no email processing functionality. The vulnerable net/mail parsing functions are not called by lpm at any point during package installation or management operations.

CVE-2026-39821 / GO-2026-5026 is the Go idna / net/http hostname validation issue, but the lpm helper only downloads from code-defined hosts. `cmd/populator/modules.go:20` and `cmd/populator/modules.go:25` hardcode the module registry URL, `cmd/populator/Populator.go:23` and `cmd/populator/Populator.go:29` show only the embedded package manifest is iterated, and the HTTP helpers consume those fixed URLs (`cmd/populator/artifactory_maven.go:28`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_maven.go:30`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_github.go:31`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_github.go:32`, `internal/app/utils/Http.go:13`, `internal/app/utils/Http.go:25`). There is no attacker-controlled hostname input path here, so the Punycode hostname-validation bug is unreachable in this deployment.

statements.status_notes: On Unix systems, opening a file in an os.Root improperly follows symlinks to locations outside of the Root when the final path component of the path is a symbolic link and the path ends in /. For example, root.Open("symlink/") will open "symlink" even when "symlink" is a symbolic link pointing outside of the root.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib os.Root symlink-following vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.12, 1.26.5, and 1.27.0-rc.2. The scanner reported affected Go stdlib version v1.26.4 in the lpm helper bundled in published Liquibase Secure Docker images (docker/Dockerfile:35, docker/Dockerfile:49) — confirmed by extracting the released liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 binary and running `go version` on it, which reports go1.26.4, matching the scanner's reported installed version exactly. The vulnerable API, os.Root (and OpenRoot), is a defensive filesystem-sandboxing API added in Go 1.24; a source-level grep of the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.5 repository for os.Root, OpenRoot, and .Root( returned zero hits, so lpm does not use the vulnerable API at all. Defense in depth: the Secure Docker entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is explicitly configured (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4); the default runtime path executes the Java Liquibase CLI directly and never calls lpm (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119-121).

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-27142 fixed a vulnerability in which URLs were not correctly escaped inside of a <meta> tag's <content> attribute. If the URL content were to insert ASCII whitespaces around the '=' rune inside of the <content> attribute, the escaper would fail to similarly escape it, leading to XSS.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib html/template escaping vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 declares go 1.25.10 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix. Defense in depth: lpm source contains no html/template usage, and the Liquibase Secure Docker entrypoint only calls lpm for optional driver installation when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4).

statements.status_notes: ReverseProxy can forward queries containing parameters not visible to Rewrite functions. When used with a Rewrite function, or a Director function which parses query parameters, ReverseProxy sanitizes the forwarded request to remove query parameters which are not parsed by url.ParseQuery. ReverseProxy does not take ParseQuery's limit on the total number of query parameters (controlled by GODEBUG=urlmaxqueryparams=N) into account. This can permit ReverseProxy to forward a request containing a query parameter that is not visible to the Rewrite function. For example, the query "a1=x&a2=x&...&a10000=x&hidden=y" can forward the parameter "hidden=y" while hiding it from the proxy's Rewrite function.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib net/http/httputil ReverseProxy query sanitization vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 declares go 1.25.10 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix. Defense in depth: lpm source contains no ReverseProxy or net/http/httputil usage, and the Liquibase Secure Docker entrypoint only calls lpm for optional driver installation when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4).

statements.status_notes: If a trusted template author were to write a <script> tag containing an empty 'type' attribute or a 'type' attribute with an ASCII whitespace, the execution of the template would incorrectly escape any data passed into the <script> block.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib html/template script escaping vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 declares go 1.25.10 (liquibase-package-manager/go.mod:3), which includes the fix. Defense in depth: lpm source contains no html/template usage, and the Liquibase Secure Docker entrypoint only calls lpm for optional driver installation when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4).

statements.status_notes: The Dial and LookupPort functions panic on Windows when provided with an input containing a NUL (0).
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib Dial and LookupPort panic vulnerability requires Windows when processing input containing a NUL byte. The assessed Liquibase Secure Docker image uses the Linux base image eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (docker/Dockerfile:2), so the vulnerable Windows runtime environment is absent.

statements.status_notes: In systemd 259, systemd-journald can send ANSI escape sequences to the terminals of arbitrary users when a "logger -p emerg" command is executed, if ForwardToWall=yes is set.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires systemd-journald to be running as a system service with ForwardToWall=yes, receiving a "logger -p emerg" invocation. A review of the running container found no systemd or systemd-journald process at all: the container has no init system, PID 1 is the Liquibase entrypoint script itself, and libsystemd0 ships only as a linked library dependency of other base-image packages, never as a running daemon. The vulnerable journald forwarding path cannot exist in a container that never runs journald.

statements.status_notes: In MIT Kerberos 5 before 1.22.3, there is a NULL pointer dereference if an application calls gss_accept_sec_context() on a system with a NegoEx mechanism registered in /etc/gss/mech. An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger this, causing the process to terminate in parse_nego_message.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libgssapi-krb5-2 1.20.1-6ubuntu2.6, below Ubuntu's fixed 1.20.1-6ubuntu2.7, but this issue requires an application to act as a GSS acceptor by calling gss_accept_sec_context() on a system with a NegoEx mechanism registered in /etc/gss/mech. Liquibase Secure is a client-side CLI image and a review of its build and stock runtime path found no use of gss_accept_sec_context or NegoEx.

statements.status_notes: In MIT Kerberos 5 before 1.22.3, there is an integer underflow and resultant out-of-bounds read if an application calls gss_accept_sec_context() on a system with a NegoEx mechanism registered in /etc/gss/mech. An unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger this, possibly causing the process to terminate in parse_message.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libgssapi-krb5-2 1.20.1-6ubuntu2.6, below Ubuntu's fixed 1.20.1-6ubuntu2.7, but this issue requires an application to act as a GSS acceptor by calling gss_accept_sec_context() on a system with a NegoEx mechanism registered in /etc/gss/mech. Liquibase Secure is a client-side CLI image and a review of its build and stock runtime path found no use of gss_accept_sec_context or NegoEx.

statements.status_notes: The iconv() function in the GNU C Library versions 2.43 and earlier may crash due to an assertion failure when converting inputs from the IBM1390 or IBM1399 character sets, which may be used to remotely crash an application. This vulnerability can be trivially mitigated by removing the IBM1390 and IBM1399 character sets from systems that do not need them.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.39-0ubuntu8.7, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.39-0ubuntu8.8, but this issue requires an application to process IBM1390 or IBM1399 encoded input through glibc's iconv conversion path. The stock Liquibase Secure runtime is the Liquibase Java CLI, and a review of its build and runtime path found no references to iconv or those IBM1390 or IBM1399 code pages.

statements.status_notes: XML External Entity (XXE) via Unsanitized Dictionary Parsing in Apache OpenNLP DictionaryEntryPersistor. Versions before 2.5.9 and before 3.0.0-M3 initialize dictionary XML parsing without secure processing or DTD restrictions, allowing attacker-supplied dictionary files to trigger local file disclosure or server-side request forgery during SAX parsing.
statements.impact_statement: OpenNLP DictionaryEntryPersistor XXE vulnerability fixed in 2.5.9. Liquibase Secure declares opennlp-tools through opennlp.version 2.5.8 (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/pom.xml:76) in the phileas AI services dependency (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:18, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:19, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/pom.xml:20), but the vulnerable dictionary XML parsing API is not imported or called. The only production OpenNLP usage found is document categorization and tokenization (tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/src/main/java/ai/philterd/phileas/service/ai/sentiment/OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java:22, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/src/main/java/ai/philterd/phileas/service/ai/sentiment/OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java:23, tools/liquibase-checks/phileas/phileas-services/phileas-services-ai/src/main/java/ai/philterd/phileas/service/ai/sentiment/OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java:24).

statements.status_notes: A local attacker on the same host as the application may be able to take control of the directory used by ApplicationTemp. When server.servlet.session.persistent is set to true and the attack persists across application restarts, this may allow the attacker to read session information and hijack authenticated users or deploy a gadget chain and execute code as the application's user.
statements.impact_statement: Spring Boot ApplicationTemp exploitation requires server.servlet.session.persistent=true and persistence across application restarts. Liquibase Secure's Docker image starts the Liquibase CLI entrypoint (docker/Dockerfile:68), and grep for server.servlet.session.persistent, ApplicationTemp, persistent=true, and setPersistent across Java, XML, properties, YAML, and YML files returned no matches.

statements.status_notes: In certain circumstances, Spring Boot's default web security is ineffective allowing unauthorized access to all endpoints. For an application to be vulnerable, it must be a servlet-based web application, have no Spring Security configuration of its own and rely on the default web security filter chain, depend on spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure, and not depend on spring-boot-health.
statements.impact_statement: Spring Boot default web security bypass requires the application to depend on spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure and not depend on spring-boot-health. The repository's only Spring Boot declaration is spring-boot-autoconfigure, provided-scope for the Pro integration (pro/pom.xml:81); grep for spring-boot-actuator-autoconfigure, spring-boot-starter-actuator, and spring-boot-health across pom.xml files returned no matches.

statements.status_notes: libexpat before 2.8.0 uses insufficient entropy, and thus hash flooding can occur via a crafted XML document.
statements.impact_statement: This hash-flooding weakness requires an application to call libexpat's parsing API on attacker-controlled XML to exploit insufficient hash-seed entropy. Liquibase Secure parses changelogs using the JVM's own bundled XML parser and never links against or calls system libexpat.

statements.status_notes: Little CMS (lcms2) through 2.18 has an integer overflow in CubeSize in cmslut.c because the overflow check is performed after the multiplication.
statements.impact_statement: Little CMS 2.18 integer overflow in CubeSize/cmslut.c. The scan reported Oracle OpenJDK 21.0.11+10-LTS, but Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1) and contains no Little CMS/lcms2 references in the repository, so the scanner's openjdk match is a false product match.

statements.status_notes: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Apache Tomcat. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117. Older, unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version [FIXED_VERSION], which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Unbounded request body reads in Tomcat WebDAV LOCK and PROPFIND handling affect Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. The license utility pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.21 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26, tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:52) through spring-boot-starter-web (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:60) and starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20), but no WebDAV servlet, WebDAV mapping, or PROPFIND/LOCK handler is configured in tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main or its application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1).

statements.status_notes: Improper Input Validation vulnerability in Apache Tomcat: HTTP/2 request headers were not validated, which may have triggered unexpected application behavior. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.117, and 10.0.0-M1 through 10.0.27. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
statements.impact_statement: HTTP/2 request header validation gap in Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires HTTP/2 connections to a running Tomcat server. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not enable HTTP/2 — application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) sets no server.http2.enabled property and declares no HTTP/2 connector, and the codebase contains no HTTP/2-specific Tomcat configuration. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26), so the fixed version is installed regardless.

statements.status_notes: Netty allows request-line validation to be bypassed when a DefaultHttpRequest or DefaultFullHttpRequest is created first and its URI is later changed via setUri(). If attacker-controlled input reaches setUri(), HttpRequestEncoder and RtspEncoder can write CRLF sequences into the request line, enabling HTTP request smuggling or RTSP request injection.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in netty-codec-http 4.1.133.Final; this repository's current build already resolves netty-codec-http 4.1.136.Final via the Azure extension's Netty HTTP client, past the fix line. This CVE requires attacker-controlled data to reach DefaultHttpRequest.setUri() before Netty emits an outbound request line. Liquibase's connection URIs are operator-configured, not supplied by untrusted end-users, and a source review found no code calling DefaultHttpRequest, DefaultFullHttpRequest, setUri(), HttpRequestEncoder, or RtspEncoder directly.

statements.status_notes: Applications that evaluate user-supplied Spring Expression Language (SpEL) expressions are vulnerable to an Algorithmic Denial of Service (DoS). By providing a specially crafted expression, an attacker can trigger excessive resource consumption during evaluation, leading to application degradation or unavailability.
statements.impact_statement: Spring Expression is a transitive dependency of spring-context, declared provided/optional at core/liquibase-standard/pom.xml:85. Repo search found no org.springframework.expression imports, no SpelExpressionParser, and no StandardEvaluationContext usage. The only parseExpression() hit is the custom tokenizer in commercial-databases/liquibase-commercial-couchbase/src/main/java/ liquibase/ext/couchbase/provider/ExpressionDocumentKeyProvider.java:38, which does not evaluate SpEL. The reactor also pins <spring.version>7.0.8</spring.version> in core/pom.xml:79.

statements.status_notes: GNU gzip contains a vulnerability in the gzexe utility related to insecure temporary file handling. When the mktemp utility is not available in the user's PATH, gzexe falls back to constructing a temporary file path based solely on the process ID. This predictable filename is created without exclusive access or existence checks. A local attacker can pre-create the predicted temporary file path as a symbolic link pointing to an arbitrary file writable by the victim. When gzexe runs, it follows the symlink and overwrites the target file.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports gzip 1.12-1ubuntu3.1, below Ubuntu's fixed 1.12-1ubuntu3.2, but this issue is specific to the gzexe wrapper when it falls back to a predictable temporary filename. Liquibase Secure does not invoke gzexe or the gzip utility in its build or stock runtime path.

statements.status_notes: GNU gzip contains a global buffer overflow vulnerability in the LZH decompression logic caused by improper reuse of shared global state between different decompression formats within a single execution. GNU gzip maintains a global array that is shared across the LZ77, LZW, and LZH decompression routines and is not reinitialized between files processed in the same invocation. By decompressing a specially crafted LZW file followed by a specially crafted LZH file in a single gzip -d command, an attacker can poison the shared global state and subsequently trigger an out-of-bounds read in the LZH decoder.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports gzip 1.12-1ubuntu3.1, below Ubuntu's fixed 1.12-1ubuntu3.2, but this issue requires a single gzip -d invocation to process a crafted LZW file and then a crafted LZH file so shared decoder state carries across formats. Liquibase Secure does not invoke the gzip utility in its build or stock runtime path.

statements.status_notes: Apache OpenNLP ExtensionLoader is vulnerable to arbitrary class instantiation via attacker-controlled input passed to the extension loading mechanism, potentially allowing remote code execution.
statements.impact_statement: Apache OpenNLP ExtensionLoader arbitrary class instantiation vulnerability. The ExtensionLoader API is not imported or called anywhere in Liquibase Secure. The only production OpenNLP usage is document categorization and tokenization via DoccatModel, DocumentCategorizerME, and WhitespaceTokenizer in OpenNLPSentimentDetector.java; no extension loading or dynamic class instantiation occurs.

statements.status_notes: pgjdbc is an open source postgresql JDBC Driver. From version 42.2.0 to before version 42.7.11, pgjdbc is vulnerable to a client-side denial of service during SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication. A malicious server can instruct the driver to perform SCRAM authentication with a very large iteration count. With a large enough value, the client spends an unbounded amount of CPU time inside PBKDF2 before authentication can fail. A single attempt ties up a CPU core. Repeated or concurrent attempts exhaust client CPU and can wedge connection pools. In affected versions, loginTimeout did not fully mitigate this problem. When loginTimeout expired, the caller could stop waiting, but the worker thread performing the connection attempt could continue running and burning CPU inside the SCRAM PBKDF2 computation. This issue has been patched in version 42.7.11.
statements.impact_statement: PostgreSQL JDBC SCRAM-SHA-256 client-side denial of service fixed in 42.7.11. Liquibase Secure distribution declares postgresql.version as 42.7.11 (dist/pom.xml:23) and uses that property for the org.postgresql:postgresql dependency (dist/pom.xml:115, dist/pom.xml:117), so the vulnerable 42.7.9 code reported by the scanner is not present in the current distribution build.

statements.status_notes: bzip2 contains an off-by-one error in the bzip2recover utility. When processing a specially crafted file, the application performs an out-of-bounds write to a global buffer, resulting in memory corruption and a crash (denial of service).
statements.impact_statement: This off-by-one flaw is specific to the bzip2recover recovery utility, not the core bzip2 compression library. Liquibase Secure's container only ever execs the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime; a review of the container's runtime path found no invocation of bzip2recover, bzip2, bunzip2, or any bzip2 API. libbz2 ships only as an inherited base-image library dependency.

statements.status_notes: Apache OpenNLP AbstractModelReader allocates unbounded memory when reading model files, allowing a malicious or malformed model file to cause an out-of-memory denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: Apache OpenNLP AbstractModelReader OOM denial-of-service vulnerability via unbounded memory allocation during model loading. Exploitation requires loading an attacker-controlled or malformed model file. Liquibase Secure bundles pre-packaged, trusted OpenNLP model files at build time; no model files are loaded from external or user-controlled sources at runtime. AbstractModelReader is not imported or called directly in Liquibase code.

statements.status_notes: Archive::Tar versions before 3.08 for Perl extract symlinks with attacker controlled targets outside the extraction directory. _make_special_file() passes the tar header's linkname to symlink() without validating it against absolute paths or .. segments. The secure-extract mode check that guards regular file extraction does not cover the symlink target. A subsequent open through the extracted name reads or writes the attacker chosen path.
statements.impact_statement: The scanner reported perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.2 and the Ubuntu fix level is 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.3. This issue requires an application to invoke Perl Archive::Tar extraction on attacker-controlled archives so a crafted symlink target is created outside the extraction directory. Liquibase Secure's stock container starts the Java CLI directly, and a review of the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no Perl invocation or Perl-based tar extraction path. The vulnerable Archive::Tar symlink-extraction path is therefore not reachable from the stock runtime.

statements.status_notes: Archive::Tar versions before 3.08 for Perl extract hardlinks to attacker controlled paths outside the extraction directory. _make_special_file() passes the tar header's linkname to link() without validating it against absolute paths or .. segments, creating a hardlink that shares the victim file's inode. A subsequent write through the extracted name modifies the victim file, and the post-extraction chmod, chown, and utime block in _extract_file() applies the tar header's mode, owner, and timestamps to the shared inode during extraction alone.
statements.impact_statement: The scanner reported perl-base 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.2 and the Ubuntu fix level is 5.38.2-3.2ubuntu0.3. This issue requires an application to invoke Perl Archive::Tar extraction on attacker-controlled archives so a crafted hardlink is created outside the extraction directory. Liquibase Secure's stock container starts the Java CLI directly, and a review of the runtime Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no Perl invocation or Perl-based tar extraction path. The vulnerable Archive::Tar hardlink-extraction path is therefore not reachable from the stock runtime.

statements.status_notes: Exposure of HTTP Authentication Header to unexpected hosts during WebSocket authentication in Apache Tomcat. Affects Apache Tomcat 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.21, 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.54, 9.0.2 through 9.0.117, 8.5.24 through 8.5.100, and 7.0.83 through 7.0.109. Fixed in 11.0.22, 10.1.55, and 9.0.118.
statements.impact_statement: Exposure of HTTP authentication headers to unexpected hosts during WebSocket authentication in Tomcat 11.x before 11.0.22. Exploitation requires a WebSocket client following an HTTP redirect during authentication. Only the license utility includes tomcat-embed-core (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:49-52); it starts a Spring Boot web application (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/java/com/liquibase/analytics/LiquibaseLicenseTracking.java:20) but does not use the Tomcat WebSocket client or server APIs. Application configuration (tools/liquibase-license-utility/src/main/resources/application.properties:1) contains no WebSocket endpoint definitions, and the codebase contains no ClientEndpoint/ServerEndpoint annotations or other WebSocket-related symbols. The utility also pins tomcat-embed-core to 11.0.22 (tools/liquibase-license-utility/pom.xml:26).

statements.status_notes: Pathological inputs could cause DoS through consumePhrase when parsing an email address according to RFC 5322.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib net/mail DoS via pathological email address inputs reaching the consumePhrase parser (RFC 5322 phrase parsing). lpm (Liquibase Package Manager) is the Go binary in the Docker image. lpm is a package manager for Liquibase extension drivers and has no email processing functionality. The vulnerable net/mail consumePhrase code path is not reachable from any lpm operation.

statements.status_notes: A malicious module proxy can exploit a flaw in the go command's validation of module checksums to bypass checksum database validation. This vulnerability affects any user using an untrusted module proxy (GOMODPROXY) or checksum database (GOSUMDB). A malicious module proxy can serve altered versions of the Go toolchain. When selecting a different version of the Go toolchain than the currently installed toolchain (due to the GOTOOLCHAIN environment variable, or a go.work or go.mod with a toolchain line), the go command will download and execute a toolchain provided by the module proxy. A malicious module proxy can bypass checksum database validation for this downloaded toolchain.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib toolchain-download checksum validation flaw fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3. The Secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 (docker/Dockerfile:35), and the only runtime invocation is `lpm add mysql --global` behind INSTALL_MYSQL (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4 and docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5). Repo-wide grep found no runtime `go build`, `go mod`, `GOTOOLCHAIN`, `GOMODPROXY`, `GOSUMDB`, `pkg-config`, or `cgo` usage, so the vulnerable toolchain-download path is not reachable.

statements.status_notes: A malicious module proxy can exploit a flaw in the go command's validation of module checksums to bypass checksum database validation.
statements.impact_statement: Go checksum-validation flaw in cmd/go only applies when the Go toolchain downloads modules or toolchains from an untrusted proxy or checksum database. Liquibase Secure installs lpm from a release ZIP (`docker/Dockerfile:39`) and the runtime entrypoint only invokes lpm to add mysql when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4`). This image does not execute `go`, use GOTOOLCHAIN, or perform module downloads at runtime.

statements.status_notes: Decoding a maliciously-crafted MIME header containing many invalid encoded-words can consume excessive CPU.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib mime.WordDecoder.DecodeHeader quadratic complexity vulnerability fixed in Go 1.25.11 and 1.26.4. Current Liquibase Secure Docker builds install lpm 0.3.4 (docker/Dockerfile:35) from the liquibase-package-manager v0.3.4 release (docker/Dockerfile:49). The Docker entrypoint only calls lpm for optional driver installation when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4). A reachability grep across docker and core found no WordDecoder.DecodeHeader, mime.WordDecoder, encoded-word, MIME header, net/mail, ReadMIMEHeader, or textproto usage, so the vulnerable MIME header decoding path is not reachable from the Liquibase Secure Docker runtime.

statements.status_notes: Handshakes which used Encrypted Client Hello could be de-anonymized by a passive network observer due to a disclosure of pre-shared key identities in the unencrypted client hello.
statements.impact_statement: Go stdlib crypto/tls Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) PSK-identity disclosure, fixed in Go 1.25.12 and 1.26.5 (GO-2026-5856). Only the latest published tag actually ships a fixed Go toolchain: extracting and inspecting the embedded Go build info of the `lpm` binary in each currently published `liquibase/liquibase-secure` tag shows 5.2.2 -> lpm 0.3.6 (go1.26.8, fixed), 5.2.1/5.2.0 -> lpm 0.3.4 (go1.26.4, unfixed), and 5.1.1/5.1.0/5.0.3/5.0.2/5.0.1 -> lpm 0.3.1/0.3.0/0.2.16/0.2.15/0.2.14 (go1.25.8/1.25.7/1.25.5/1.25.3/1.25.1, all unfixed). The current source tree's docker/Dockerfile:35 pins a newer lpm 0.3.7, itself also built with go1.26.8 (fixed) per the SHA256-pinned release artifact (lpm-0.3.7-linux.zip, sha256 329eafbe9289d1e83a62cb89844ac461bb5b9d4c5f5f184c8f26244e350e8a95). Despite most published tags running an unfixed Go toolchain by version, the vulnerable handshake path requires the TLS client to opt in by setting `crypto/tls.Config.EncryptedClientHelloConfigList` -- ECH support has been opt-in-only since its introduction in Go 1.23 (see the Go 1.23 release notes: "This feature can be enabled by setting the Config.EncryptedClientHelloConfigList field"). lpm's only HTTP client (internal/app/utils/Http.go) has been an unmodified bare `http.Client{}` with no custom Transport or tls.Config across every released version checked (v0.2.14 through v0.3.7), and no import of crypto/tls or reference to ECHConfigList exists anywhere in lpm's source or dependency tree. ECH is therefore never negotiated by lpm in any published Secure image, regardless of the underlying Go version, so the vulnerable code path is not reachable in any of them.

Netty epoll native transport vulnerability fixed in 4.2.13.Final. statements.status_notes: An issue was found in Python's tarfile module. statements.impact_statement: Liquibase Secure bundles a GraalPy-based embedded Python runtime so that customers can author custom policy-check scripts with full access to the Python standard library, including tarfile. Triggering this issue requires a customer to deliberately author and configure their own custom check script that imports tarfile and extracts an untrusted archive; Liquibase creates no such exposure on its own, and no shipped check performs this action.

statements.status_notes: Calling gethostbyaddr or gethostbyaddr_r with a configured nsswitch.conf that specifies the library's DNS backend in the GNU C Library version 2.34 to version 2.43 could, with a crafted response from the configured DNS server, result in a violation of the DNS specification that causes the application to treat a non-answer section of the DNS response as a valid answer.
statements.impact_statement: glibc gethostbyaddr/gethostbyaddr_r DNS-response-parsing bug (CWE-125), exploitable when a crafted response from the configured DNS resolver causes the application to treat a non-answer section as a valid answer. It is used purely for cosmetic/ attribution fields (DATABASECHANGELOGLOCK owner in LockDatabaseChangeLogGenerator, license/run-context tracking, drift report hostname), never for access control or trust decisions. Exploitation therefore requires a compromised or MITM'd DNS resolver already configured and trusted by the deployment (via /etc/resolv.conf and nsswitch.conf's "dns" hosts backend) -- not an arbitrary remote attacker. statements.status_notes:
Issue summary: A specially crafted PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed message could trigger a use-after-free during PKCS#7 signature verification.
Impact summary: A use-after-free may result in process crashes, heap corruption, or potentially remote code execution.
When processing a PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed message, if the SignedData digestAlgorithms field is present as an empty ASN.1 SET, OpenSSL may incorrectly free a caller-owned BIO during PKCS7_verify(). A subsequent use of the BIO by the calling application results in a use-after-free condition.
In the common case this occurs when the application later calls BIO_free() on the BIO originally passed to PKCS7_verify(). Depending on allocator behavior and application-specific BIO usage patterns, this may result in a crash or other memory corruption. In some application contexts this may potentially be exploitable for remote code execution.
Applications that process PKCS#7 or S/MIME signed messages using OpenSSL PKCS#7 APIs may be affected. Applications using the CMS APIs for this processing are not affected.
The FIPS modules in 4.0, 3.6, 3.5, 3.4, and 3.0 are not affected by this issue, as the affected code is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

The vulnerable path is not reachable: a focused grep for PKCS7_verify, PKCS7_, PKCS7, PKCS#7, S/MIME, SMIME, smime, BIO_free, and digestAlgorithms across repository sources returned zero hits.

statements.status_notes: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. This bypasses standard bailiwick rules, where a server authoritative for a subdomain should not be trusted to provide authoritative records for its parent. statements.status_notes: channelBinding=require connections can be silently downgraded from SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS with channel binding to plain SCRAM-SHA-256 without it. This is therefore not reachable in Liquibase's *default* configuration, but is reachable if a user opts into channelBinding=require. Independently, the current source already pins the fix by default: pom.xml:62 sets postgresql.version to 42.7.13, and dist/pom.xml:123 consumes that managed version — the scanner reported 42.7.11 on the published 5.2.0 image (built before this version bump).

statements.status_notes: jackson-databind contains the general-purpose data-binding functionality and tree-model for Jackson Data Processor. From 2.10.0 until 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4, jackson-databind's PolymorphicTypeValidator (PTV) is the primary safety mechanism guarding polymorphic deserialization. When polymorphic typing is enabled and a type identifier contains generic parameters (i.e. the type ID string contains <), DatabindContext._resolveAndValidateGeneric() validates only the raw container class name (the substring before <) against the configured PTV. If the container type is approved, the method parses the full canonical type string via TypeFactory.constructFromCanonical() and returns the fully parameterized type without ever validating the nested type arguments against the PTV. The nested type arguments are then resolved, instantiated, and populated as beans during deserialization. An attacker who controls the type ID can therefore place a denied class as a generic type parameter of an allowed container — for example java.util.ArrayList<com.evil.Gadget> when only java.util.ArrayList is allow-listed. The container passes the PTV check; com.evil.Gadget is loaded via Class.forName(name, true, loader), instantiated, and its properties are set from attacker-controlled JSON. This completely bypasses an explicitly configured PTV allow-list. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.18.8, 2.21.4, and 3.1.4.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. In versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final, the SpdyHttpDecoder handler in Netty's SPDY-to-HTTP codec allocates a pooled ByteBuf when processing a client-initiated SYN_STREAM frame and stores the partially constructed FullHttpRequest in messageMap; when the remote peer sends RST_STREAM for that stream, or the accumulated content exceeds maxContentLength, the decoder removes the entry without releasing the pooled ByteBuf, leading to native memory exhaustion. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: The real vulnerable code is Netty's legacy SPDY-to-HTTP codec (SpdyHttpDecoder), not generic HTTP/2 handling — confirmed against the GitHub Security Advisory. Neither liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain nor liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty ever negotiates or wires an SPDY codec; both only ever speak HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2, so SpdyHttpDecoder is never reached by either. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final via the AWS SDK chain, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth; Azure's copy remains on the vulnerable 4.1.135.Final and relies solely on the SPDY-never-used argument.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final are affected by a logical-operator error in CorsHandler's origin evaluation that allows the shortCircuit() security control to be bypassed entirely by sending a request with an Origin: null header, forwarding unauthorized cross-origin requests to the backend application. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: CORS enforcement is inherently server-side, and neither module ever runs an HTTP server: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty both only ever make outbound client requests, so CorsHandler is never reached by either. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. In versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final, a remote unauthenticated peer can leak one direct ByteBuf per HTTP/2 DATA frame in applications that enable HTTP/2 content decompression via DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener: when a DATA frame is processed for a stream whose decompressor has already been closed, the retained buffer is not released on the error path, eventually exhausting direct memory and crashing the JVM. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: netty-codec-http2's DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener DATA-frame handling is exercised by both modules' outbound HTTP/2 clients: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain, and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty. Exploiting the leak requires a malicious or misbehaving HTTP/2 peer; both modules only ever connect to a single trusted, TLS-authenticated first-party endpoint (AWS Secrets Manager for Cassandra, Microsoft Azure services for Azure), so the same "requires a malicious peer, and we only talk to a trusted endpoint" argument applies to both. Cassandra's copy also happens to already resolve at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth; Azure's copy remains on the vulnerable 4.1.135.Final and relies solely on the trusted-endpoint argument.

statements.status_notes: When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads a few bytes from each new connection to see if they contain the HTTP/2 client preface. ReadHeaderTimeout is unexpectedly not being applied when doing this.

Liquibase Secure is a database migration CLI, not an HTTP server. The secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50) and only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5), so the server-side unencrypted HTTP/2 listener required by the advisory is absent.

statements.status_notes: sqlparse is a non-validating SQL parser module for Python. Prior to 0.6.0, SQL_REGEX in sqlparse/keywords.py and the per-position loop in sqlparse/lexer.py repeatedly scan unmatched dollar-quoted literal and multiline-comment delimiters, causing quadratic CPU consumption through sqlparse.parse(), sqlparse.format(), and sqlparse.split(). statements.impact_statement: sqlparse is pinned at 0.5.3 in tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:864. The surrounding build plugin comment states these Python packages are only needed at build time and are never used at runtime (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:893, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/pom.xml:895), and the runtime implementation only references sqlparse in explanatory comments about a possible Python lock hang (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/main/java/com/liquibase/executor/PythonScriptExecutor.java:77, tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/main/java/com/liquibase/executor/PythonScriptExecutor.java:240). The only actual import is in a test fixture (tools/liquibase-checks/liquibase-checks/src/test/resources/scripts/badScript.py:4). NVD and GitHub both describe this as a sqlparse DoS fixed in 0.6.0, but the vulnerable parser is not reachable from the Liquibase runtime.

statements.status_notes: sqlparse is a non-validating SQL parser module for Python. Prior to 0.6.0, sqlparse/filters/output.py fails to escape existing backslashes before quotes in sqlparse.format output_format='python' and output_format='php' and the corresponding sqlformat -l modes, allowing crafted SQL to terminate the generated string and inject Python or PHP code when a downstream consumer executes or imports the generated source. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.0.
statements.impact_statement: sqlparse ships in the runtime virtual environment of the checks module's embedded Python scripting engine, which end users can use to author custom check scripts; the build only strips pip, setuptools, and their installer machinery from that environment, not sqlparse itself. None of the check scripts Liquibase bundles and runs by default import sqlparse — they use a different SQL parsing library for changeset SQL. The vulnerable Python/PHP output-formatting code path (sqlparse.format with output_format='python' or 'php') is only reachable if a customer authors and configures their own custom check script that imports sqlparse and calls it in one of those modes; no shipped configuration does this out of the box.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, the newHandshakeResponse methods of WebSocketServerHandshaker07 and WebSocketServerHandshaker08 complete a WebSocket protocol upgrade based solely on the presence of a Sec-WebSocket-Version: 7 (or 8) header, without verifying the mandatory Connection: Upgrade and Upgrade: websocket headers, enabling HTTP request smuggling / protocol-confusion attacks through intermediaries that don't recognize the request as an Upgrade. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: WebSocketServerHandshaker07/08 are server-side handshake classes, and neither module ever runs a WebSocket server: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty each only make plain HTTPS client calls, never WebSocket connections. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, HttpContentEncoder maintains a per-channel acceptEncodingQueue that accumulates attacker-controlled data without a size limit; the queue is filled on the I/O thread for every inbound HTTP request and drained only when the application writes a non-1xx response, allowing an attacker to exploit HTTP/1.1 pipelining to exhaust resources. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: HttpContentEncoder encodes outbound responses on the server side of an HTTP exchange, a role neither module ever plays: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty each only make outbound client requests and decode inbound responses, never run an HTTP server. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, Netty's HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.x translation layer (Http2StreamFrameToHttpObjectCodec / InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapter) fails to deduplicate or validate Host headers when an HTTP/2 client supplies both the :authority pseudo-header and a literal host header in a single HEADERS frame, producing an HttpRequest with two differing Host headers that can be used to bypass request-routing logic. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE concerns the HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.x translation layer a front-end server or proxy uses (e.g. InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapter) to receive and translate inbound HTTP/2 requests — a server/proxy-side concept neither module ever exercises, both being pure outbound HTTP/2 clients: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty each only ever act as a direct HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 client, never a protocol-translating front end. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http2 also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. In versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final, Bzip2Decoder's run-length encoding (RLE) state machine can enter an infinite loop when processing a malformed bzip2 stream, permanently occupying the event-loop thread at 100% CPU and causing denial of service. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.

No Liquibase Netty consumer adds Bzip2Decoder/Bzip2Encoder to a pipeline.

In versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final, Bzip2Decoder's run-length encoding (RLE) state machine can enter an infinite loop when processing a malformed bzip2 stream, permanently occupying the event-loop thread at 100% CPU and causing denial of service. statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final, io.netty.handler.codec.http.cors.CorsHandler's setVaryHeader method replaces application-defined Vary headers (such as Authorization or Cookie) with Origin. This allows a caching proxy or CDN sitting in front of a server using CorsHandler to reuse one user's authenticated response for another user, disclosing sensitive information. Fixed in versions 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final.
statements.impact_statement: CorsHandler applies CORS response headers on the server side of an HTTP exchange; this repository never runs an HTTP server that uses it. A source review found no references to CorsHandler or CorsConfig anywhere in this repository's own code; every module that bundles netty-codec-http does so only as a transitive dependency of an outbound HTTP client (the AWS SDK's netty-nio-client, the Azure SDK's azure-core-http-netty, the Couchbase Java client, and the Cassandra driver's own AWS SDK chain), never as a server. The AWS extension and the Cassandra extension already resolve netty-codec-http at 4.1.137.Final, past the fix line, as defense-in-depth; the Azure extension remains on the vulnerable 4.1.135.Final and the Couchbase client's shaded copy remains on 4.2.16.Final, both relying solely on the reachability argument.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, HttpPostRequestEncoder constructs multipart HTTP request bodies by directly concatenating user-supplied filenames and field names into Content-Disposition MIME headers without validating or sanitizing CRLF characters. Since MIME headers are delimited by CRLF, an attacker who controls the filename can inject arbitrary MIME headers into the multipart body part. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: Fixed in netty-codec-http 4.1.136.Final per NVD and GHSA. This repository's current build already resolves netty-codec-http 4.1.136.Final via the Azure extension's Netty HTTP client, past the fix line. This CVE is specific to Netty's HttpPostRequestEncoder multipart body construction from attacker-controlled filenames and field names, but this repository's only multipart upload implementation (S3 object uploads in the AWS extension) uses the AWS SDK's REST-level multipart API (separate part-numbered PUT requests), not Netty's multipart/form-data encoder — a fundamentally different mechanism. A source review found no references to HttpPostRequestEncoder, DiskFileUpload, MemoryFileUpload, or MixedFileUpload anywhere in this repository, so the vulnerable encoder path is not reachable regardless of version.

Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with logon to the infrastructure where Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition executes to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.
statements.impact_statement: Oracle Java SE/GraalVM Install-component vulnerability, fixed upstream in 21.0.12 (Oracle August 2026 CPU). The flaw is in Oracle's Java installer, a packaging component that ships only with Oracle's own distribution. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1) via docker-entrypoint.sh (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8); Temurin's JRE is unpacked from a release archive, not installed through Oracle's installer, so the vulnerable component is not present in the image at all. There is no Adoptium/Temurin tracking entry for this CVE. Unlike the other Oracle Java SE entries in this batch (sandbox/Web Start applicability mismatches, justified requires_environment), this is a component absence -- the installer isn't shipped at all -- hence code_not_present.

statements.status_notes: When verifying the password-based MAC protection of a CMP message, OpenSSL reads the protectionAlg algorithm parameter with X509_ALGOR_get0() and treats the returned value as a PBMParameter after checking only that the pointer is not null, without validating the ASN.1 type. A remote attacker can crash an application acting as a CMP server that accepts PBM-protected messages, or a CMP client talking to a malicious or intercepted CMP server, causing a denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.29, but this issue is only reachable when an application verifies CMP password-based protection on attacker-supplied messages. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL CMP tooling, and a source review found no references to CMP, PBM, or OSSL_CMP request-processing paths in the product runtime.

statements.status_notes: Calling wordexp with WRDE_APPEND in the GNU C Library version 2.0 to version 2.43 can cause the interface to return invalid memory in the we_wordv member, which on subsequent calls to wordfree may abort the process.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to call glibc's wordexp function with the WRDE_APPEND flag. Neither the JVM nor the container's bash entrypoint calls wordexp; this is a C-language shell-word-expansion API that Liquibase Secure's Java and bash-only runtime path never invokes.

statements.status_notes: When asked to both use a .netrc file for credentials and follow HTTP redirects, libcurl could leak the password used for the first host to the followed-to host under certain circumstances.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.24, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to combine .netrc credential loading with HTTP redirect following. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for its own downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no libcurl, .netrc, or redirect-handling path in the container build or runtime entrypoint.

statements.status_notes: Apache HttpComponents Client, when using the classic (blocking) I/O model, fails to release the underlying connection back to the connection manager if the response contains an invalid or unsupported Content-Encoding header value. Repeated requests to a malicious or misbehaving server leak connections and eventually exhaust the connection pool, producing a denial of service. The async I/O model is not affected. Fixed in version 5.6.3.
statements.impact_statement: httpclient5 is already pinned to 5.6.4 (past the 5.6.3 fix), but that alone only holds until a future downgrade, so we also checked reachability of the classic (blocking) client this CVE affects. Two usages exist: a bundled PII-detection filter, which is unreachable - it requires a policy-loading path Liquibase's checks engine never invokes - and the AWS SDK's synchronous Secrets Manager client, which is real but only ever talks to AWS's own TLS-authenticated endpoint. Exploitation needs that server to repeatedly send malformed Content-Encoding responses, so a remote attacker can't trigger this without already controlling or intercepting trusted AWS traffic - the same precondition used for the related Netty HTTP/2 CVEs.

statements.status_notes: Improper Access Control, Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat leads to security constraint bypass if a constraint for a longer path is specified before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58, 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Security constraint bypass when a `<security-constraint>` for a longer path is declared before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path in web.xml. Requires an active Tomcat servlet container evaluating security constraints against deployed web.xml descriptors. Liquibase is a CLI tool that uses picocli for command-line parsing and never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No servlet container is started, so no security-constraint evaluation ever occurs.

statements.status_notes: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator. If, before windowSize requests have been made, a client makes a DIGEST authenticated request with a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the replay window then that request is replayable once only while the associated nonceCount remains within the replay window. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fix the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Authentication bypass by capture-replay in Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator: a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the replay window can be replayed once before it ages out. Requires an active Tomcat servlet container with DIGEST authentication configured and processing inbound authenticated requests. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No DIGEST authenticator is ever configured or invoked.

statements.status_notes: Expat through 2.8.3 contains a denial of service vulnerability caused by quadratic algorithmic complexity in the storeAtts() function in xmlparse.c, where processing N specified attributes with non-normalized values triggers an O(N^2) linear scan of elementType->defaultAtts to determine CDATA status. A remote unauthenticated attacker can supply a single well-formed XML document of a few megabytes to an application parsing untrusted XML to cause excessive CPU consumption, resulting in denial of service.
statements.impact_statement: This denial-of-service flaw requires an application to call libexpat's XML_Parse API on attacker-controlled XML with many non-normalized attributes. Liquibase Secure parses changelogs using the JVM's own bundled XML parser and never links against or calls system libexpat; the library ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: When expanding paths that begin with a tilde followed by a username, glibc's parse_tilde allocates the extracted username on the stack with strndupa based on untrusted input length. If an application passes attacker-controlled input to wordexp, an excessively long username can exhaust stack space and trigger a stack clash.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.35-0ubuntu3.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.35-0ubuntu3.15, but this flaw requires an application to pass attacker-controlled input into glibc's wordexp path-expansion API. The stock Liquibase Secure runtime is the Liquibase Java CLI behind a bash-based entrypoint, and a source review found no references to wordexp or WRDE_APPEND in the container build or runtime path.

statements.status_notes: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's FORM authentication process allows the bypassing of a security constraint that limits user access to a resource via POST but not GET. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.
statements.impact_statement: Incorrect Authorization in Tomcat's FORM authentication process allows bypassing a security constraint that limits a user to POST access on a resource (not GET). Requires an active Tomcat servlet container with FORM authentication and a POST-only security constraint configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No FORM authenticator or security constraint is ever configured.

statements.status_notes: Successfully using libcurl to do a transfer over one HTTP proxy with Digest authentication and then changing the proxy host for a second transfer while reusing the same handle can cause libcurl to pass the Proxy-Authorization header intended for the first proxy to the second.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.24, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to reuse the same handle across multiple proxy hosts with Digest authentication enabled. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no proxy-authenticated libcurl flow, Digest-proxy handling, or curl handle reuse path in the container build or runtime entrypoint.

statements.status_notes: libexpat before 2.8.3 has an out-of-bounds read and resultant infinite loop because low surrogates are treated the same as high surrogates during Unicode processing in the *_toUtf16 functions.
statements.impact_statement: This out-of-bounds read requires an application to call libexpat's internal *_toUtf16 Unicode conversion functions on attacker-controlled surrogate pairs. Liquibase Secure parses changelogs using the JVM's own bundled XML parser and never links against or calls system libexpat.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, io.netty.handler.codec.dns.AbstractDnsRecord, io.netty.handler.codec.dns.DefaultDnsRecordDecoder.decodeRecord(), and io.netty.handler.codec.dns.DnsCodecUtil.decompressDomainName() failed to release retained or newly allocated ByteBuf objects when IDN.toASCII() or encodeDomainName() rejected a malformed domain name, allowing unauthenticated remote DNS packets to leak direct memory incrementally until denial of service. Fixed in 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
statements.impact_statement: netty-resolver-dns:4.1.135.Final (below the 4.1.136.Final fix line) resolves for this module via reactor-netty-http:1.2.18 -> reactor-netty-core:1.2.18, and unlike the other Netty CVEs assessed here, is genuinely wired into every outbound connection by default via reactor-netty-core's NameResolverProvider — this is not a code-not-reachable case. The hostname resolved is always operator-supplied configuration, never derived from changelog content: Key Vault modifiers parse the vault host from a Liquibase configuration value, and Blob Storage access uses a separately configured storage-account property, so an attacker can't inject a resolution target purely via a malicious changelog. That only rules out attacker-chosen domains, though — it doesn't rule out this CVE's actual mechanism, a malformed DNS response to an otherwise-legitimate query. DNS isn't TLS-authenticated the way this module's HTTP/2 traffic is, so the "trusted endpoint" argument used for the HTTP/2 CVEs on this module doesn't transfer here. Exploitation requires network-level access to the deployment's DNS resolution path — an assumption about the deployment environment this codebase can't verify. No newer reactor-netty release exists yet with a fixed Netty.

statements.status_notes: A signed integer overflow when sizing the destination buffer for Unicode output in ASN1_mbstring_ncopy can lead to a heap buffer overflow. The issue requires an application to call ASN1_mbstring_copy or ASN1_mbstring_ncopy directly, or to register a custom string type via ASN1_STRING_TABLE_add with attacker-controlled input large enough to overflow the size calculation.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.25, but this issue requires an application to call OpenSSL's ASN1_mbstring_copy or ASN1_mbstring_ncopy APIs directly, or to register a custom string type and then feed it extremely large attacker-controlled input. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL string-processing APIs, and a source review found no references to those OpenSSL ASN.1 entry points in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final, io.netty.handler.ssl.SslClientHelloHandler#decode checks the wrong offset before reading the four-byte TLS handshake header, so a ClientHello whose handshake header spans records can cause an IndexOutOfBoundsException and invoke select(ctx, null). This selects the default SslContext instead of the SNI-specific context. In deployments where per-SNI clientAuth=REQUIRE is the sole mutual TLS gate, the default SslContext uses clientAuth=NONE or clientAuth=OPTIONAL, and no application-layer certificate verification exists, an unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass the protected route's mutual TLS requirement. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final.
statements.impact_statement: SslClientHelloHandler#decode checks the wrong offset before reading the four-byte TLS handshake header, so a ClientHello whose handshake header spans records can throw IndexOutOfBoundsException and fall back to the default SslContext instead of the SNI-specific one. This only becomes an mTLS bypass in a deployment that (a) runs a Netty server accepting inbound TLS connections, (b) uses per-SNI SslContext selection as the sole mutual-TLS gate (clientAuth=REQUIRE on the SNI context, weaker on the default), and (c) has no application-layer certificate check. Liquibase never runs a Netty server: a grep across all Java sources for ServerBootstrap, NioServerSocketChannel, SniHandler, AbstractSniHandler, and SslClientHelloHandler returns zero hits: netty-handler is present only as a transitive dependency of outbound HTTP/TLS clients (Azure SDK's azure-core-http-netty, the AWS SDK, the Couchbase client, the Cassandra JDBC driver). The scanner found netty-handler below the fixed versions in five bundled jars (Docker Scan run https://github.com/liquibase/liquibase-pro/actions/runs/34365994421): liquibase-commercial-cassandra.jar 4.1.119.Final, liquibase-azure.jar 4.1.135.Final, liquibase-aws-extension.jar 4.1.136.Final, liquibase-commercial-couchbase.jar 4.2.16.Final, and liquibase-azure-deps.jar (unlabeled in the scan, same shaded copy as liquibase-azure.jar); none of them run a Netty server, so the version gap does not matter to this assessment.

statements.status_notes: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final, the default SniHandler constructors use pre-handshake ClientHello aggregation implemented in SslClientHelloHandler, which repeatedly recopies all previously received bytes each time it processes another fragment of a ClientHello split across TLS records. An unauthenticated attacker can advertise a large ClientHello and deliver it in thousands of tiny records, causing quadratic CPU consumption on the event loop and degrading TLS handling for other clients. Fixed in versions 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final.
statements.impact_statement: This CVE affects the same pre-handshake ClientHello aggregation code in SslClientHelloHandler as CVE-2026-75595, already assessed in this file: a server-side SNI-routing feature that repeatedly recopies buffered bytes while reassembling a fragmented ClientHello, causing quadratic CPU consumption when an attacker splits a large ClientHello across many small TLS records. This only matters to a deployment running a Netty server with per-SNI SslContext selection (SniHandler/AbstractSniHandler). A source review found no references to ServerBootstrap, NioServerSocketChannel, SniHandler, AbstractSniHandler, or SslClientHelloHandler anywhere in this repository; netty-handler is present only as a transitive dependency of outbound HTTP/TLS clients (the AWS SDK's netty-nio-client, the Azure SDK's azure-core-http-netty, the Couchbase Java client, and the Cassandra driver's own AWS SDK chain), none of which run a Netty server. The AWS extension already resolves netty-handler at 4.1.137.Final, past the fix line, as defense-in-depth; the Azure extension remains on 4.1.135.Final, the Cassandra extension on 4.1.130.Final, and the Couchbase client's shaded copy on 4.2.16.Final, all relying solely on the reachability argument.

statements.status_notes: For ChaCha20-Poly1305 and AES-OCB, EVP_Cipher could report successful decryption for an empty ciphertext without verifying the supplied AEAD tag. Applications that rely on EVP_Cipher to validate the tag in that case might accept forged messages.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libssl3 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.19, below Ubuntu's fixed 3.0.2-0ubuntu1.29, but this issue requires an application to use OpenSSL's EVP_Cipher one-shot API for ChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-OCB decryption on an empty ciphertext while expecting that call to validate the AEAD tag. Liquibase Secure's stock container runs the Liquibase Java CLI rather than OpenSSL AEAD decryption helpers, and a source review found no references to EVP_Cipher, ChaCha20-Poly1305, or AES-OCB in the product runtime path.

statements.status_notes: The nsenter --join-cgroup option opens the target cgroup.procs file as root and leaves that file descriptor open across later namespace and credential changes and across execve(). Because the kernel checks later cgroup migrations using the credentials from the original open, a program run in an attacker-controlled target can inherit root's ability to move host processes between cgroups. After a privileged operator uses --join-cgroup against that target, an unprivileged user can migrate and terminate unrelated root processes.

statements.status_notes: When CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY is configured alongside options that disable standard peer verification (CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER = 0 and CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST = 0), libcurl fails to enforce public key pinning on connections established without a presented server certificate, allowing unauthenticated connections to succeed when they should be rejected.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to configure libcurl with CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY alongside disabled peer verification options. Liquibase Secure's runtime process tree never links against libcurl; curl ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: Converting crafted EUC_JISX0213 input to UCS-4 or the internal wide character encoding, for example with iconv, in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to 2.44 may result in the converter making no progress, causing the calling application to hang.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.35-0ubuntu3.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.35-0ubuntu3.15, but this issue requires an application to feed attacker-controlled EUC_JISX0213 data through glibc's iconv conversion path with a small enough output buffer to split a two-code-point decode. Liquibase Secure's stock runtime path is the Java CLI, and a review of its build and runtime flow found no references to iconv or EUC_JISX0213 processing. The vulnerable glibc conversion path is not reachable from Liquibase Secure.

statements.status_notes: When libpsl support is enabled, libcurl fails to enforce the Public Suffix List boundary check when processing a Set-Cookie header where the Domain attribute explicitly matches an origin host that is itself a public suffix. Instead of coercing it into a strict host-only cookie, libcurl saves the cookie with wildcard domain scope, inappropriately including it in subsequent outbound requests or HTTP redirects to arbitrary sibling subdomains under the same public suffix.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to build libcurl with libpsl support and process attacker-controlled Set-Cookie responses. Liquibase Secure's runtime process tree never links against libcurl; curl ships only as an inherited base-image package and is never invoked at container runtime.

statements.status_notes: Pod::Text versions before 6.1.1 for Perl allow CPU and memory exhaustion formatting a POD document whose =over nesting drives the margin to the output width. Each =over adds its indent to the margin, which wrap() subtracts from the output width to get the space available for text. When that space reaches zero, the line-splitting substitution matches the empty string, and the loop consumes no input while appending the margin padding on every pass. Formatting an attacker-supplied POD document never returns, and the output grows until memory is exhausted.
statements.impact_statement: Pod::Text (bundled with perl-base) CPU/memory exhaustion formatting a crafted POD document. Nothing in this repository or docker-entrypoint.sh shells out to perl or invokes POD formatting (pod2text/perldoc); the entrypoint does its own pattern matching with bash case/glob syntax.

statements.status_notes: A new transfer that uses STARTTLS to upgrade the connection might reuse an existing live connection even though the TLS configuration mismatches and the connection should not have been reused.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports curl 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.20, below Ubuntu's fixed 7.81.0-1ubuntu1.25, but this issue requires a libcurl-based application to upgrade a connection with STARTTLS and then incorrectly reuse a live connection whose TLS settings no longer match. Liquibase Secure's stock container uses wget for its own downloads and executes the Liquibase Java CLI at runtime, and a focused review found no STARTTLS, curl connection-pool, or libcurl TLS-reuse path in the container build or runtime entrypoint.

statements.status_notes: sqlparse is a non-validating SQL parser module for Python. Prior to 0.6.0, sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True) and sqlformat --reindent route attacker-controlled parenthesized tuple lists through ReindentFilter._get_offset() in sqlparse/filters/reindent.py, where _flatten_up_to_token() repeatedly rebuilds and joins the statement prefix. Thousands of offset calculations walk an expanding token tree, producing quadratic CPU consumption for inputs that remain below MAX_GROUPING_TOKENS and causing request delays, reduced throughput, or worker starvation. This issue is fixed in version 0.6.0.
statements.impact_statement: sqlparse ships in the runtime virtual environment of the checks module's embedded Python scripting engine, which end users can use to author custom check scripts; the build only strips pip, setuptools, and their installer machinery from that environment, not sqlparse itself. None of the check scripts Liquibase bundles and runs by default import sqlparse — they use a different SQL parsing library for changeset SQL. The vulnerable reindent code path (sqlparse.format(sql, reindent=True) or sqlformat --reindent) is only reachable if a customer authors and configures their own custom check script that imports sqlparse and calls it in that mode against attacker-influenced SQL; no shipped configuration does this out of the box.
